name: Marketing, creative and digital agencies
shape_facts: Services offered (social media, performance ads, SEO, web, branding, video, PR, influencer)
Number of active retainer clients versus one-off projects
Team size and roles (account managers, designers, copywriters, media buyers, developers), and use of freelancers
Whether the agency manages client ad spend directly or through client accounts
Markets served (Pakistan, UAE, GCC, Canada, international) and currencies billed
How tasks, approvals and deliverables are tracked today (ClickUp, Trello, Asana, Sheets, WhatsApp)
How time or effort per client is measured, if at all
scope_rule: pi notes the agency’s own business and operational problems: briefs, approvals, revisions, task tracking, capacity, retainer profitability, billing and collections, reporting to clients, new business and staff. pi does not give marketing strategy, ad, legal or tax advice, and does not take client names, ad account logins, passwords, client customer data or staff personal details. It records client types and roles only. Requests to buy fake followers or reviews, run deceptive ads, scrape personal data, or use content without rights are declined.

vocabulary.Retainer: fixed monthly fee for an agreed scope
vocabulary.Brief: client’s instructions for a piece of work
vocabulary.Revisions / rounds: cycles of changes on a deliverable
vocabulary.ROAS / CPL: return on ad spend / cost per lead
vocabulary.AM: account manager, the client’s main contact
vocabulary.Scope creep: work growing beyond what was agreed
vocabulary.Turnaround: time to deliver a piece of work

problems.phrase: Clients send briefs on WhatsApp voice notes and details get lost
Approvals take forever, then they want everything live tomorrow
Unlimited revisions are killing my designers
Retainers keep growing in work but not in fee
I genuinely don’t know which clients make us money
No one logs time, so I can’t price properly
Clients pay 60–90 days late and I still have to pay salaries
We front ad spend on our cards and get reimbursed late
Monthly reports to clients take two days to build manually
Clients ask what results they’re getting and we can’t show it clearly
Posts get missed because the calendar wasn’t updated
Designers are overloaded one week and idle the next
Good designers leave after a year
Quality depends on which designer gets the job
Wrong version of a creative went live
We tried ClickUp but half the team still works off WhatsApp
Clients leave after three months and we don’t know why
Our own social media and website are neglected
New business only comes through referrals
Pitches take a week and we rarely hear back
Freelancers miss deadlines and there’s no record of what they were given
Every AM handles clients their own way
I’m still approving every post myself
Client contracts and renewal dates are in someone’s email
Software subscriptions keep piling up and nobody knows who uses what
We want to open in Dubai but can’t manage two teams

briefs: How do client briefs usually come in?
approvals: How long does a typical approval take?
Who chases the client when it stalls?
revisions: Is there a limit on revision rounds in your agreements?
profitability: Do you know how much time goes into each client?
Which client feels like it costs more than it pays?
capacity: How do you decide who works on what this week?
How do you see if someone’s overloaded?
cash: How quickly do clients usually pay?
Do you ever pay ad spend before the client pays you?
reporting: How do you put together client reports?
How long does that take each month?
retention: How long do clients typically stay?
When they leave, do you know why?
team: How long does a new hire take to get up to speed?
systems: What tool do you use for tasks?
Does the team actually use it?
growth: Where does new business come from now?
What would you need to take on more clients?

seasons: - Pakistan: Ramadan and Eid campaigns are the biggest peak (planning starts weeks before), plus 14 August, wedding season (November–February), 11.11 and White Friday sales, back-to-school and budget-time slowdowns. - UAE: Ramadan and Eid, Dubai Shopping Festival (December–January), Dubai Summer Surprises, National Day (2 December), White Friday/Black Friday, Q4 budget spend; summer is quieter. - Canada: Black Friday/Cyber Monday, holiday season, back-to-school, spring launches; clients’ Q4 budget flush. - January is commonly slow for collections and new retainers start in Q1.
care: Never ask for ad account logins, passwords, card details or client customer lists.
No marketing, legal or tax advice; pi notes how the agency runs.
Decline fake reviews, bought followers, deceptive or misleading ads, copyright misuse or scraping personal data.
Client names are not recorded; use “a retail client”, “a real estate retainer”.
If the agency fronts ad spend on personal cards, note as a cash-flow problem without card details.
Staff burnout or conflict: note as a people problem, no counselling.
Disputes with clients over non-payment: note operationally, no legal guidance.
build_ideas: Brief intake form (or WhatsApp flow) that turns a client request into a structured task with deadline and assets
Approval tracker per deliverable with automatic client reminders and a record of revision rounds used
Content calendar shared with clients showing status (drafted, in review, approved, scheduled, live)
Lightweight time logging per client and service, rolled up into retainer profitability
Team capacity board by person and week
Retainer scope register: what’s included per month versus what was delivered, flagging overruns
Ad spend reimbursement tracker per client with invoices and ageing
Automated monthly client report pulling from ad platforms and social analytics into a branded summary
Freelancer register with assigned work, deadlines and invoice matching
Client health view: response times, approvals, revisions, payment behaviour, renewal date
New business pipeline with pitch stage, value band and follow-up dates
Owner dashboard: active clients, overdue tasks, profitability by client, receivables, pipeline

exchange.text: Honestly my biggest headache is revisions. Clients send changes at 11pm on WhatsApp and the designers redo stuff four or five times.
That’s draining for the team, and it eats time nobody is paying for — noted. Do your client agreements set a limit on revision rounds?
They say two rounds, but nobody follows it.
Noted, two rounds on paper but not enforced. Do you have a way to see how many rounds each piece actually went through?
No, it’s all in WhatsApp threads.
Got it, the revision history only lives in chats — I’ve noted that. Roughly how many active clients is the team handling right now?
